title: Liturgy, Iambus, and the Cast-Iron Hand
source: Original interpretation of Zamyatin We Record Nine; original dramatic prose; no copied passages
content_note: Non-graphic depiction of a public execution

scenes.title: 01 · Sixty-Six Rings of Glass
scenes.speaker: D-503 · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE VOICE
scenes.line: All these faces turn toward one center. Surely that must mean we share one purpose.
scenes.story: On a brilliant day, D-503 joins the crowds seated in sixty-six concentric rings around the Cube. The silence and tightly ordered bodies evoke an ancient religious gathering, though he sees the One State as a rational replacement for religion.
scenes.observation: The narrator describes tiered seating, disciplined spectators, and a solemn public gathering.
scenes.inference: An orderly crowd establishes every person's freely chosen moral agreement.
scenes.question: What does the geometry actually show?
choices: A public arrangement and coordinated behavior.
Independently verified consent by every spectator.
reply: Correct: this statement preserves the limit of the observed narrative.
That conclusion is not established by the evidence in the record.

scenes.title: 02 · The Number Taken Away
scenes.speaker: NARRATOR · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE VOICE
scenes.line: The man stands below the platform without the badge that once named him.
scenes.story: A condemned poet waits at the base of the Cube with his identifying badge removed and his hands restrained. His vulnerability stands in stark contrast to the multitude around him. The State describes the occasion as collective victory.
scenes.observation: An identified human has been condemned, restrained, and stripped of his numerical badge.
scenes.inference: The State's chosen language resolves the morality of the sentence.
scenes.question: Whose loss must the witness preserve?
choices: The condemned person's humanity and imminent loss.
Only the State's abstract category of disobedience.
reply: Correct: this statement preserves the limit of the observed narrative.
That conclusion is not established by the evidence in the record.

scenes.title: 03 · The Cast-Iron Hand
scenes.speaker: D-503 · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE VOICE
scenes.line: A single raised hand directs all of us as though we were a mechanism.
scenes.story: The Benefactor stands near the Machine above the plaza. His large, heavy hands command the event through gestures. D-503 interprets his authority as the mathematical expression of countless wills, but that endorsement is D-503's belief.
scenes.observation: The Benefactor directs the ceremony; D-503 reveres his authority.
scenes.inference: Centralized force proves democratic consent or moral legitimacy.
scenes.question: What does the hand signify as an observation?
reply: Correct: this statement preserves the limit of the observed narrative.
That conclusion is not established by the evidence in the record.

scenes.title: 04 · Steel Over Fire
scenes.speaker: NARRATOR · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE VOICE
scenes.line: One poet turns the State's history into triumphant rhythm.
scenes.story: A State poet recites a public work praising machines and law as conquerors of chaos. The crowd receives an officially approved narrative in which technological power restores order. Poetry serves the institution's self-description.
scenes.observation: Public verse praises the State's victories over chaos.
scenes.inference: Artistic eloquence establishes the justice of the cause it celebrates.
scenes.question: What is poetry doing here?
choices: Communicating and legitimizing an official narrative.
reply: Correct: this statement preserves the limit of the observed narrative.
That conclusion is not established by the evidence in the record.

scenes.title: 05 · The Poet He Knows
scenes.speaker: D-503 · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE VOICE
scenes.line: It is R-13. Why does my friend look so unlike himself?
scenes.story: R-13 appears as the second commissioned poet. He recites the condemned man's supposedly sacrilegious offense against the Benefactor. He finishes pale, looking away. D-503 glimpses a sharp triangular face beside him, but cannot establish the private significance of either impression.
scenes.observation: R-13 performs and appears distressed; D-503 notices a fleeting face.
scenes.inference: R-13's visible distress proves an entire political commitment.
scenes.question: What remains unknown?
choices: His reasons for discomfort and the identity or purpose of the fleeting observer.
That R-13 was present and spoke.
reply: Correct: this statement preserves the limit of the observed narrative.
That conclusion is not established by the evidence in the record.

scenes.title: 06 · An Execution Behind Technology
scenes.speaker: NARRATOR · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE VOICE
scenes.line: The mechanism is precise; the consequence is irreversible.
scenes.story: The Benefactor operates the Machine, and the condemned poet is executed. The original narrative uses technological imagery to describe the destruction. This cartoon interpretation shows a closed shutter and extinguished light rather than the act or aftermath.
scenes.observation: An execution takes place by order of the State.
scenes.inference: Technical precision makes the action ethically acceptable.
scenes.question: What must not be erased?
choices: A human death under institutional authority.
The humanity of the condemned person.
reply: Correct: this statement preserves the limit of the observed narrative.
That conclusion is not established by the evidence in the record.

scenes.title: 07 · After the Silence, Applause
scenes.speaker: D-503 · ORIGINAL INTERPRETIVE VOICE
scenes.line: The crowd calls it cleansing. I feel it too, yet that feeling is only mine.
scenes.story: The audience celebrates the Benefactor and Guardians. Women present flowers, and D-503 reports a sense of purification, interpreting the display as evidence of the State's rational power. This is the narrator's emotional resolution, not independent proof of collective consent or justice.
scenes.observation: Cheers, floral homage, and D-503's relief follow the execution.
scenes.inference: Public celebration retrospectively justifies taking a life.
scenes.question: What should the witness preserve?
choices: The ceremony, the death, and the narrator's interpretation as separate roots.
An equation proving state power and justice identical.
reply: Correct: this statement preserves the limit of the observed narrative.
That conclusion is not established by the evidence in the record.
